title: Peter Village: Early Woodland Enclosure in Fayette County
summary: In Fayette County, Peter Village is a large Early Woodland ditch-and-embankment enclosure, likely a gathering place where people worked minerals.
bodyMarkdown:
In Fayette County, Peter Village (15Fa166) is a huge Early Woodland ditch-and-embankment enclosure—about 9.2 hectares, irregular rather than a neat geometric circle. Long mislabeled an Adena “village,” it is better read as a specialized gathering and craft place; archaeologist Berle Clay tied it to barite and galena working, and newer geoarchaeology (Henry and others) points to dual embankments and construction as early as the 5th century BCE—among the earliest monumental enclosures in the Middle Ohio Valley. It is one of the Bluegrass ritual landscapes built centuries before forts and stations.
Source: [Peter Village enclosure, Squier and Davis 1848, Plate XIV](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Peter_Village_enclosure_Squier_and_Davis_Plate_XIV_Figure_3.jpg)
